payload.title: Santorini vs Mykonos for Your Wedding
payload.excerpt: Choosing between a Santorini or Mykonos wedding is a choice between two settings, not two standards.
key_takeaways: Santorini weddings face the caldera from cliff-top terraces, while Mykonos weddings sit on beaches and bays such as Ornos, Psarou and Agios Ioannis.
Ceremony type narrows the shortlist on both islands, because each venue states its own options, from terraces and a winery on Santorini to whitewashed chapels on Mykonos.
Both islands have their own airport, and Smartraveller warns that ferries can be delayed or cancelled in strong winds, so guests should plan their arrival with time to spare.
The Australian paperwork is the same whichever island you choose, starting with proof that neither of you is already married, such as a Certificate of No Impediment.

faq.q: Is Santorini or Mykonos better for a wedding?
faq.a: It depends on the setting, the ceremony and the week you want for your guests. Santorini suits a cliff-top ceremony facing the caldera; Mykonos suits a beach, a chapel by the sea and a town close by. Both have hotel venues that host weddings.

faq.q: Can we marry legally on either island?
faq.a: The Australian documents are the same for both, starting with proof that neither of you is already married, such as a CNI. Ask the authority that will marry you which documents it needs and which must be legalised.

faq.q: How do guests get to Santorini and Mykonos?
faq.a: Each island has its own airport, with flights from Athens and Thessaloniki. Ferries and large catamarans carry most visitors to the Greek islands, but services can be delayed or cancelled in strong winds.

faq.q: When can we marry on each island?
faq.a: Neither island has its own HNMS station, so the same Naxos figures guide both. At Naxos, July and August average under one rain day a month, and Smartraveller warns of frequent summer heatwaves and wildfires from June to September.

faq.q: Is a wedding on Santorini or Mykonos more expensive?
faq.a: Cost turns on your guest count, your venue and its spaces, whether you take over a whole hotel, and when you travel. Several venues publish wedding brochures, including Canaves, Santa Marina and Andronis, and your inclusions should be set out in writing before you commit.
